To be agonizingly clear, the context of this quote was people talking about imagining things in the future, and noting that even though the singularity is confusing, it's possible to imagine things beyond it - like heists.

This is also just a straight up great writing prompt - what would it mean to steal something in a post-singularity future? Who is the team? What are the security systems? How do the police work? great stuff!  Session was chatham house so I can't name who said it.

The single most useful take I heard at The Curve was "we can still heist the Mona Lisa after the singularity". There's a subtle/important point here, where some things (e.g, n of 1 goods where originally is valuable) will retain/grow in value even as everything changes.
